title: Thrombopoietin Receptor Agonists Therapy in Aplastic Anaemia.
journal: Indian journal of hematology & blood transfusion : an official journal of Indian Society of Hematology and Blood Transfusion
abstract: Immune-mediated aplastic anaemia (IAA) remains a life-threatening disorder characterized by immune-driven bone marrow failure and consequent cytopenias. Frontline therapy includes immunosuppressive therapy (IST) with horse antithymocyte globulin (h-ATG) or rabbit ATG (r-ATG) in combination with cyclosporine, or allogeneic stem cell transplantation in eligible patients. Despite these approaches, overall response rates (ORR) to IST remain at approximately 60-70%,(Complete Responses ~20-30%, Partial Responses~30-40%) with relapse and refractoriness posing major clinical challenges. Attempts to intensify IST using agents such as cyclophosphamide, mycophenolate mofetil, sirolimus, alemtuzumab, or prolonged cyclosporine(CSA) have shown limited additional benefit, suggesting that inadequate marrow reserve rather than persistent autoreactivity may underlie refractoriness. Over the past decade, thrombopoietin receptor agonists (TPO-RAs) have emerged as important therapeutic options for IAA, demonstrating single-agent activity as well as synergistic efficacy when combined with ATG and cyclosporine. Their mechanistic rationale extends beyond megakaryopoiesis. TPO receptors are expressed on hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), and TPO-RAs may enhance stem-cell viability, promote multilineage hematologic recovery, and increase marrow cellularity. Additionally, TPO-RAs may modulate immune tolerance by expanding regulatory B and T cells, attenuating macrophage activity, and impairing dendritic-cell maturation, thereby helping to rebalance immune dysregulation. Eltrombopag(EPAG) and romiplostim are the most extensively studied TPO-RAs in IAA. Eltrombopag, an oral small-molecule TPO-RA, has demonstrated efficacy in both frontline and refractory IAA, with good hematologic recovery and potential iron-chelating effects. Romiplostim, a peptibody, has been primarily used in patients with refractory disease. Their distinct pharmacokinetic and safety profiles, including concerns about hepatotoxicity with eltrombopag and potential risks of clonal evolution with long-term TPO-RA exposure, require careful clinical consideration. Prospective studies, including the NIH cohort and the RACE trial, have provided pivotal evidence that adding a TPO-RA to standard IST improves hematologic responses and supports enhanced multilineage recovery with acceptable safety. However, rates of relapse and clonal evolution remain comparable to historical cohorts. Ongoing studies aim to refine optimal sequencing, dosing strategies, and combination regimens. The evolving evidence supports the integration of TPO-RAs into IAA management to augment marrow recovery and achieve more durable correction of cytopenias.

title: Behavioral Processes Underlying Oxytocin-Induced Group Cohesion in Free-Ranging Horses.
abstract: Oxytocin, a neuropeptide hormone, has been suggested to contribute to group cohesion. However, previous studies have primarily focused on interactions at the individual or dyadic level, leaving limited direct evidence regarding how oxytocin influences behavior within established social groups. In this study, we examined the effects of intranasal oxytocin administration on social interactions in a feeding context (i.e. affiliative co-feeding or competition over spatially distributed food patches) in semi-free-ranging captive horse groups. Specifically, we asked two questions: first, which types of social interactions are altered by oxytocin; and second, whether these effects depend on individuals' social positions within the group, namely centrality and dominance. We used drone recording and machine-learning-based tracking to detect co-feeding in the same food patch and approaches toward occupied patches, while aggression was recorded through direct behavioral observation. The results showed that oxytocin affected the tolerance of approaches according to pre-existing affiliative relationships but did not consistently affect active approaches or aggression. Specifically, oxytocin redistributed social tolerance from strongly affiliated partners toward more weakly affiliated partners. By contrast, we found no consistent evidence that the effects of oxytocin depended on individuals' centrality or dominance. This study emphasizes the importance of examining oxytocin effects on social interactions in established groups, in addition to traditional dyadic paradigms. The combination of drone-based observation and machine-learning-based tracking provides a high-resolution framework for quantitative comparative analyses, which should advance our understanding of the behavioral processes through which oxytocin shapes social organization.

title: Discrepancy between cross-neutralizing reactivity and protection in horses suggests inactivated vaccine antisera underestimate cross-protection against equine influenza.
abstract: For equine influenza vaccine strain selection, antisera collected from infected horses (post-infection antisera) have been used for antigenic analysis. However, inactivated whole-virus vaccines are widely administered to horses, and therefore, the use of antisera collected from horses immunized with inactivated viruses (inactivated vaccine antisera) has the potential to be more clinically relevant for evaluating vaccine efficacy. The objective of this study was to determine whether inactivated vaccine antisera can serve as a reliable surrogate for post-infection antisera and whether they are appropriate for equine influenza vaccine strain selection. In the virus neutralization assay, post-infection antisera against a Japanese vaccine strain (A/equine/Ibaraki/1/2007) cross-reacted with the heterologous challenge strain (A/equine/New York/1/2017), whereas inactivated vaccine antisera showed a more than 10-fold reduction in cross-reactivity. However, in the experimental challenge study with A/equine/New York/1/2017, horses immunized with inactivated A/equine/Ibaraki/1/2007 showed significantly reduced rectal temperature, virus shedding, and inflammation marker levels, despite low cross-neutralizing reactivity, when compared to the unimmunized control horses. These results indicate that a reduction in cross-neutralizing reactivity of inactivated vaccine antisera does not necessarily reflect a loss of vaccine efficacy in horses. In conclusion, this study suggests that relying only on inactivated vaccine antisera underestimates vaccine efficacy against equine influenza. Although preparing post-infection antisera presents practical difficulties, their use remains valuable for the selection of appropriate vaccine strains.

title: Recombinant equine lubricin is safe and well tolerated following multiple intra-articular injections in healthy fetlock joints.
abstract: To assess the safety of recombinant equine lubricin (rEqLub) injections in healthy equine fetlocks using clinical, biochemical, and histological outcomes. 6 adult horses were enrolled (3geldings, 3mares) in a block randomized, controlled experimental study. All 24 fetlocks were assigned to receive an injection of either 2 mL rEqLub (1mg/mL) or PBS at 1 of 3 time points. Recombinant equine lubricin was injected into a randomized forelimb at 28 days and 1 day prior to study completion, and rEqLub and PBS were injected into contralateral hindlimbs at 7 days prior to study completion. Clinical and orthopedic examinations were performed at baseline and prior to and 1 day following each injection; synovial fluid was collected for biochemistry, flow cytometry, and proteomics; synovial membrane and osteochondral sections were collected from day-28 rEqLub-treated joints and scored using Osteoarthritis Research Society International criteria. 3 sequential IA injections of rEqLub in 3 different healthy fetlocks were well tolerated and did not result in adverse clinical or histologic outcomes. There were no differences in clinical or synovial fluid biochemical parameters between rEqLub- and PBS-injected joints. Synovial fluid WBC concentrations and total protein were increased 1 day after injection in rEqLub-treated joints. IA rEqLub did not cause any detectable clinical, biochemical, or histological adverse effects, supporting the favorable tolerability and safety profile of rEqLub. The small sample size and multijoint design are limitations. rEqLub injections were well tolerated, establishing a basis for future equine efficacy trials to evaluate the ability of recombinant lubricin to mitigate osteoarthritis in a clinically relevant equine model.

title: AI-driven, qualitative GC-MS/MS-based endogenous steroid profiling with automated classification for sex cohort determination.
abstract: The proper identification of sex cohorts is essential for anti-doping within the regulatory framework for horse racing, as investigations could be compromised if the sex of a stallion, mare or gelding were misclassified. The single-threshold approach is not very useful for assessing hormonal profiles in horses because of nonlinear relationships among testosterone and other hormones and metabolites. In the present study, an automated Steroid Detection System (SDS) was developed using PDF-based data extraction and characteristic qualitative metabolic profiles and peak intensity patterns obtained by GC-MS and utilized in AI driven model. A total of 291 post-race urine samples from Males (n = 122), Females (n = 102), and Geldings (n = 67) collected at Seoul Racecourse, Korea, were analyzed by GC-MS/MS in multiple reaction monitoring MRM mode. IS-normalized ratios of 10 key biomarker compounds were used as input features. The Random Forest (300 decision trees, balanced class weighting) had a 5-fold stratified cross-validation accuracy of 90.7 ± 2.3% with per-class accuracies of 98.4% (Male), 87.3% (Female) and 82.1% (Gelding). On a stratified held-out test set (n = 45), it achieved 95.3% accuracy, F1-score of 0.95, and AUC of 0.98, outperforming Logistic Regression (81.4%, 0.80, 0.85), Decision Tree (84.7%, 0.84, 0.88), SVM (87.2%, 0.87, 0.92), and Gradient Boosting (93.1%, 0.93, 0.97). The feature importance analysis showed that 5α-androstane-3β,17α-diol (EN3), testosterone (EN1) and nandrolone (EN4) were the most important classifiers with 61.2% of the signal. Multivariate steroid profiling using IS normalization and Random Forest is a powerful, automated tool for gender determination in horses for regulatory anti-doping control.

title: Case Report: Incidental finding of a perforating wooden foreign body in the jejunum during surgical treatment of colic in a horse: use of intraoperative infrared thermography.
abstract: Equine gastrointestinal tract perforation by a foreign body is a rare cause of colic. Assessment of intestinal viability during exploratory laparotomy is crucial and is usually performed using subjective parameters (color, motility, pulse). Infrared thermography (IRT) offers an objective, noninvasive method for assessing tissue surface temperature in real time, as it correlates with local blood perfusion. In this case, a 13-year-old Italian Saddle mare was admitted with a 24-h history of acute, progressive abdominal pain unresponsive to medical therapy. Clinical examination revealed severe discomfort, systemic compromise (HR: 53 bpm, CRT > 3 s), marked leukocytosis (16,600 cells/mm3), hyperproteinemia (8 g/dL), and severe hyperlactatemia (15 mmol/L). Transabdominal ultrasound confirmed small intestinal distention. Emergency exploratory laparotomy revealed a 10 cm solid, irregular mass in the jejunum, causing obstruction and localized perforation. Intraoperative infrared thermography (FLIR ThermaCam E8) was used at three time points (T0: exteriorization, T1: margin selection, T2: pre-repositioning) to monitor surface temperature distributions. At T0, a distinct thermal gradient (Delta T = 1.9 °C) was detected between the viable intestinal segments (mean T = 35.1 °C) and the affected ischemic area (mean T = 33.2 °C). Based on the clinical examination and findings, a segmental enterectomy with end-to-end anastomosis was performed. Post-resection mapping (T2) confirmed equal perfusion of both stumps with a difference between measurements of: Delta T = 0.1 °C. Dissection of the resected mass revealed a wooden stick. The mare recovered uneventfully and was discharged 10 days after surgery. This case demonstrates that foreign body-associated intestinal perforation should be considered among the differential diagnosis of horses presenting with severe small intestinal colic. Furthermore, intraoperative infrared thermography proved to be an adjunctive method for real-time quantification of surface temperatures in the examined stumps, providing an objective assessment of surface temperature patterns to complement visual inspection during tissue evaluation.

title: Mechanical nociceptive thresholds of the foot do not change following anaesthesia of the digital flexor tendon sheath in horses.
authors: de Da Cunha Marina Souza Luz
abstract: The selectivity of diagnostic analgesia of the digital flexor tendon sheath (DFTS) in horses remains debated. This study aimed to determine whether intrasynovial administration of 2% lidocaine into the DFTS increases the mechanical nociceptive threshold (MNT) of the dorsal lamellar stratum, sole, coronary band and heel bulbs, with correct placement confirmed by contrast tenography. Six healthy horses with no clinical or radiographic distal limb abnormalities were used. Forelimbs were randomly assigned, with one limb receiving 2% lidocaine and the contralateral limb receiving lactated Ringer's solution via the palmar pastern approach to the DFTS; both solutions were mixed with radiographic contrast to confirm accurate placement. MNT was measured in 10-foot regions using a portable pressure dynamometer before and at predefined time points up to 4 hours after DFTS injection. Data were compared using Friedman and Wilcoxon tests (p < 0.05). No significant differences in MNT were observed over time or between groups. MNT values rarely exceeded 1-kg force, and medians in both groups showed only minor fluctuations, remaining close to 0.5-kg force across the evaluated foot regions. Under the conditions of this study, contrast-confirmed intrasynovial administration of 2% lidocaine into the DFTS did not produce detectable desensitisation of the evaluated foot regions in clinically normal horses.

title: Prolonged wireless measurement of intragastric pH and pharmacodynamics of extended-release injectable omeprazole in horses.
abstract: Adaptation of wireless capsules for intragastric pH measurement in horses has a short, variable attachment duration. Prolonged measurement is important for pharmacodynamic studies. Extended-release injectable omeprazole (ERIO) induces acid suppression for ≤ 7 days. Five-day dosing intervals are now recommended for improved healing rates. To (1) optimize the methodology to achieve 5-7 days of capsule attachment; (2) determine whether capsules can detect a treatment effect of ERIO; and (3) describe the pharmacodynamics of ERIO. Twelve healthy adult horses. Capsules were attached transendoscopically to the glandular mucosa on day 0 using either 1 hemostasis clip (1HEM; n = 4), 4 hemostasis clips (4HEM; n = 5), or a helix tacking device (TACK; n = 9). Intragastric pH was continuously recorded and ERIO was administered on day 1. Data are reported as median (IQR). Capsules remained attached and obtained data for 51 h (42-65), 129 h (105-256), and 95 h (71-154) for 1HEM, 4HEM, and TACK, respectively. The percentage of time the pH was above 4 (%tpH > 4) was significantly higher (P 4 exceeded 66% for 5 days after ERIO in 4/6 horses (66.7%). These refined, minimally invasive attachment techniques enabled longer, more consistent intragastric pH measurement. A treatment effect associated with ERIO administration was detected and %tpH > 4 exceeded 66% throughout the 5-day dosing interval in most horses.

title: Metagenomics analysis reveals horse feces as a reservoir of putative ARG-like sequences.
abstract: Despite the widespread distribution of horses and their close interface with human environments, the equine antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) reservoir remains insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to comprehensively elucidate the equine resistome by analyzing 104 equine fecal metagenomes sampled across China, thereby establishing a critical baseline for antimicrobial stewardship in equine husbandry. Through a non-redundant gene catalog approach, we identified 3,264 unique ARG-related coding sequences (CDSs). To detect distant homologs, hidden Markov model (HMM) profiling was applied, revealing 2,420 putatively novel ARG-like sequences. Functional classification indicated that over 90% of these sequences mediate resistance through antibiotic inactivation or target protection, whereas efflux and impaired penetration accounted for less than 10%. Taxonomic profiling attributed these predicted sequences to 23 phyla and 146 genera, with Firmicutes, Bacteroidetes, and Proteobacteria identified as the detected taxa. Furthermore, we identified 731 plasmid-associated ARG-like candidates, of which 446 is novel variants, predominantly conferring resistance to macrolides, streptogramins, aminoglycosides, and β-lactams. Experimental validation confirmed that the novel gene abc-f(9) significantly reduced macrolide susceptibility in vitro, elevating the tilmicosin minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of Escherichia coli from 64 to 256 μg/mL. These findings provide the first systematic characterization of the equine ARG repertoire, significantly expanding the known global resistome. Our results offer a foundational resource for assessing the risks of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) transmission and implementing informed surveillance strategies in horse farming.

title: Venezuelan equine encephalitis, Mayaro and chikungunya viruses as causative agents of febrile syndrome in Colombian patients during 2013 and 2014.
journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases
abstract: Colombia's tropical climate and low-altitude cities create an ideal environment where mosquito-borne diseases can thrive. During 2013-2014, dengue was the most diagnosed cause of febrile syndrome. However, other viruses like Venezuelan equine encephalitis (VEEV), Mayaro (MAYV), and chikungunya viruses (CHIKV) were also present, and their true prevalence was likely underestimated due to limited surveillance. We conducted a cross-sectional study involving 90 febrile malaria- and dengue-negative patients from the Urabá region. For each patient, we collected both acute and convalescent serum samples, which were analyzed to detect antibodies against VEEV, CHIKV, and MAYV. Additionally, we attempted virus isolation from the acute-phase serum samples. We found that antibodies against VEEV were present in 28.3% of samples, CHIKV antibodies were detected in 5%, and MAYV antibodies in 1.7%. Notably, one patient seroconverted against CHIKV even before the first outbreak was recognized in Colombia in 2014. Furthermore, we isolated and fully sequenced VEEV, and our analysis revealed a close phylogenetic relationship with subtype ID Panamanian strains. This study highlights the need to consider arboviruses beyond just dengue (DENV), when evaluating febrile illness in Colombia. The detection of VEEV and CHIKV, even before they were officially recognized as significant public health threats in this region, underscores the need for enhanced surveillance and diagnostic capabilities.

title: Commercially available objective gait evaluation systems show good to excellent reliability in horses across hard-surface types and multiple operators.
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
abstract: To evaluate the intrasystem reliability of an AI-based smartphone application Sleip (AI-SPA), the inertial measurement unit (IMU) system Equinosis Q Lameness Locator (LL), and the IMU system Equisym (ES) across 2 different hard surfaces and to assess the interoperator reliability for the 2 IMU systems. 8 mixed-breed research horses, aged 4 to 12 years, with varying degrees of gait asymmetries were utilized. To assess intrasystem reliability, horses were in-hand, straight-line trotted on either epoxy-coated concrete or rubber-coated concrete. Three trials were performed for LL and ES, while 6 concurrent trials were performed for AI-SPA. Interoperator reliability was assessed with 4 operators on the rubber-coated concrete only. Intraclass correlation coefficients and SE of measurements were calculated for 4 outcome parameters common to all systems as well as a variety of system-specific outcome parameters for LL and ES. Nearly all intraclass correlation coefficients indicated moderate to excellent intrasystem reliability (> 0.50) across the 3 systems (AI-SPA, 0.40 to 0.85; LL, 0.73 to 0.94; ES, 0.44 to 0.99) and were comparable between surfaces. Interoperator reliability was moderate to excellent for both LL (0.72 to 0.92) and ES (0.73 to 0.96). Standard error of measurement values remained relatively stable across study conditions. Despite inherent horse variability and minor differences in testing conditions, objective gait evaluation systems consistently produced measurements indicating moderate to excellent reliability and low measurement error. These findings indicate that observed changes in system output are unlikely to be impacted by operator or hard-surface effects, supporting clinical reliability of these systems in routine practice when utilizing manufacturers' instructions.

title: Standardized reference sera: advancing harmonization of equine viral arteritis serologic testing across national reference laboratories in the European Union.
journal: Journal of veterinary diagnostic investigation : official publication of the American Association of Veterinary Laboratory Diagnosticians, Inc
abstract: Equine viral arteritis is a contagious disease affecting equids, caused by equine arteritis virus (EAV). Accurate serologic testing is essential for surveillance, breeding management, and international trade. The virus neutralization test (VNT), prescribed by the World Organisation for Animal Health, remains the gold standard, but variability in quantitative results between laboratories limits harmonization. We aimed to produce and validate standardized EAV-positive reference sera to improve VNT consistency across European Union national reference laboratories, and to assess their impact on interlaboratory proficiency testing (IL-PT). Three sera from a vaccinated pony and one from a naturally infected horse were produced and evaluated for reproducibility, homogeneity, and stability. These sera were first distributed during an IL-PT campaign in 2013 to allow participants to characterize them and define expected titers and acceptance ranges. Once established, the sera were reused in subsequent IL-PT campaigns (2016, 2020, 2024) as positive controls. All reference sera had strong reproducibility, homogeneity, and stability. Their use was associated with an improvement in interlaboratory performance, with results within expected ranges increasing from 51.1% in 2013 to 81.7% in 2024. These standardized sera offer a robust tool for harmonizing EAV VNTs, improving test reliability, and supporting surveillance and trade.

title: Rare allergen sources are clinically relevant sensitizers in Central Europe.
abstract: In recent times, diagnosing allergies apart from house dust mite (HDM), birch tree, and grass pollen has become increasingly difficult because allergen manufacturers have withdrawn many commercial skin prick test (SPT) solutions for rare allergen sources. A cohort of 5,857 patients (mean age 35.9 ± 20.3 years, 60.5% female) was tested with standardized SPT panels comprising 46 inhalant and food allergens at a large allergy outpatient clinic in Vienna. Cases with positive tests and allergen-specific history were judged as "relevant", those without as "latent". In the patient cohort, 48.8% presented with a history of allergic rhinoconjunctivitis (ARC), 16.7% with bronchial asthma (BA), 13.2% with atopic dermatitis (AD), and 28.9% with food allergy (FA). Of 113,893 SPTs, 7.0% were relevant, 5.3% were latent, and 87.7% remained negative. The 3 most frequent allergen sources - grass, birch, and HDM - showed the highest ratio of 22.2% relevant compared to 7.1% latent SPTs. The 6 other non-rare allergen sources - European ash tree, mugwort, ragweed, Alternaria alternata, cat, and dog - yielded 9.5% positive and 7.4% latent SPT results. The other 34 rare allergen sources resulted in 1.8% positive and 3.9% latent tests. Plantain, horse, hazelnut (food), soymilk, peanut, plane tree, and nettle ranked top among the rare allergens. Among rare allergens, relevant SPTs to horse/rabbit, Alternaria alternata, oat flour, and rye flour were associated with an increased risk for BA including work-related asthma. 15.4% (1,230/7,985) of all relevant SPTs were observed in "rare allergens". This demonstrates the necessity of including rare allergens in standard allergy workups.

title: Fungal DNA in pooled equine uterine samples: an exploratory ITS2 amplicon sequencing pilot study.
abstract: Fungal DNA in the equine uterus remains poorly characterized, particularly in mares without overt clinical uterine disease. This exploratory pooled pilot study used ITS2 amplicon sequencing to describe fungal DNA profiles in pooled uterine samples and to perform descriptive comparisons by subsequent pregnancy outcome and sampling method. Conventional microbiological culture findings were summarized as clinical context. samples were collected during naturally occurring estrus and, in mares that were subsequently mated, before the first mating of the studied estrous cycle. Low-volume uterine lavage (LVL) samples from 12 naturally mated Trakehner mares were pooled by outcome into a pregnant-LVL pool (1FR; n = 5) and a non-pregnant-LVL pool (2NFR; n = 7). The paired sampling-method comparison comprised a paired LVL pool (3LVL) and a paired SWAB pool (4SWAB), each constructed from samples collected from the same five mares. After bioinformatic processing, 82,862-130,870 reads and 27-111 final unique amplicon sequence variants were retained per pooled library. ITS2-target quantitative PCR detected 1,107-1,728 target copies/μL of pooled DNA extract. Neither the extraction blank nor the library-preparation blank crossed the qPCR detection threshold within 40 cycles; however, both yielded sequencing reads, and sequence-resolved control analysis could not exclude low-level laboratory or sequencing-related contamination. A targeted sensitivity analysis excluding the sequence feature shared by the library-preparation blank and two biological libraries did not materially alter the descriptive taxonomic composition, diversity, or ordination patterns. Ascomycota predominated across the pooled libraries (50.7-72.5%), followed by Basidiomycota (8.1-24.1%). The pregnant-LVL library had the lowest pool-level Shannon diversity value and occupied an ordination position that differed from the other libraries primarily along the first principal coordinate. The paired LVL and swab libraries also differed descriptively in taxonomic composition and ordination position. No fungal growth was reported in the available routine culture reports. These observations demonstrate the presence of diverse fungal DNA signals but do not establish viable uterine colonization, fungal infection, an association with subsequent pregnancy outcome, or equivalence between sampling methods. Confirmation requires sequencing of individual mares, comprehensive field and laboratory controls, standardized mycological culture, and integration with cytological, histopathological, and reproductive data.

title: Subcutaneous abscessation: An atypical presentation of Rhodococcus equi infection in a group of foals.
abstract: Integumentary manifestations of Rhodococcus equi infection in foals are infrequently reported in the literature. Subcutaneous abscessation as the primary clinical presentation in temporally clustered cases of foal rhodococcosis in an equine farm has not, to the authors' knowledge, been previously described. To describe an outbreak of R. equi infection where foals presented with subcutaneous abscessation as the primary clinical sign. Clinical case series. Three Thoroughbred foals aged 6-11 weeks developed subcutaneous abscesses over a 3-week period in July 2024, out of a cohort of 11 foals. Thoracic ultrasound examination was performed on all foals on the farm, and 6/11 (54%) had evidence of subclinical pneumonia. No foals other than the three cases with subcutaneous abscesses were clinically affected. Purulent aspirates from abscesses in two foals were subjected to microbiological diagnosis and yielded a pure culture of R. equi. Two of the three clinically affected foals received 4 weeks of systemic antimicrobial treatment, and all abscesses resolved. Whole-genome sequencing of one isolate demonstrated near identity to a previous UK isolate associated with pulmonary rhodococcosis, and did not reveal genetic features that could explain the atypical presentation. Financial constraints on the farm precluded microbiological confirmation of diagnosis in the third foal. Sequencing of a single isolate precluded assessment of strain relatedness within the outbreak. R. equi infection should be considered in foals presenting with subcutaneous abscesses, even in the absence of overt respiratory signs. Exposure-related factors likely contributed to this presentation, and the possibility of a transcutaneous route of entry should be considered.

title: PLEKHG5 promotes equine herpesvirus type 1 replication and is associated with changes in cellular autophagy.
abstract: Equine herpesvirus type 1 (EHV-1) is an important equine pathogen that causes respiratory disease, abortion, and neurological disorders, posing a significant threat to the equine industry worldwide. Cellular autophagy plays important roles in viral infection; however, the involvement of PLEKHG5 in EHV-1 infection and its relationship with autophagy remain poorly understood. In this study, baby hamster kidney-21 (BHK-21) cells and Syrian golden hamsters were used to investigate the role of PLEKHG5 in EHV-1 infection. The results showed that PLEKHG5 expression positively correlated with EHV-1 replication. PLEKHG5 overexpression promoted viral genome replication, titers, and protein expression, whereas PLEKHG5 knockdown significantly inhibited viral replication. Changes in PLEKHG5 expression were accompanied by alterations in the autophagy-related markers LC3 and p62 and in autophagy-related structures. Confocal microscopy revealed spatial overlap of PLEKHG5 with p62, mRFP-LC3, and LAMP1, suggesting an association with autophagy- and lysosome-related compartments. In vivo experiments demonstrated that PLEKHG5 knockdown reduced viral loads in multiple tissues and alleviated inflammatory responses and tissue damage. Collectively, these findings suggest that PLEKHG5 promotes EHV-1 replication and is associated with changes in autophagy-related processes, providing new insights into host-virus interactions.

title: B-mode ultrasonographic evaluation of normal thyroid gland in Turkmen horses: morphometric assessment and echographic characteristics.
journal: Veterinary research forum : an international quarterly journal
abstract: The thyroid gland is an integral part of the complex anatomy of the equine neck. Trans-cutaneous ultrasonography provides a non-invasive method for assessing the thyroid glands parenchyma and dimensions in horses. This study evaluated 30 clinically healthy Turkmen horses whose health status was confirmed through comprehensive physical examination, complete blood count, serum biochemical analysis, and thyroid hormone analysis. The horses were divided into two age groups: Group 1 under 36 months (three males and eight females), and Group 2: Thirty-six months and older (eight males and eleven females). Ultrasonographic assessment of the thyroid region was performed using a high-frequency linear transducer. Each thyroid lobe was systematically evaluated for its dimensions, volume, morphology, contour, parenchymal echogenicity and echotexture. Statistical analysis revealed no significant age-related differences in thyroid parameters; however, sex-based differences were observed: females had significantly greater thyroid lobe length and volume on both the left and right sides compared to males. Qualitative B-mode ultrasonography showed consistent morphological features; in the longitudinal view, all thyroid lobes exhibited a flattened, oval shape. On transverse images, most lobes (83.93%, n = 47) appeared elliptical, while the remaining lobes (16.07%, n = 9) were spherical. Irrespective of shape, all thyroid lobes demonstrated regular contour margins. Regarding echogenicity, most lobes were hyperechoic, with a few being isoechoic, relative to the sternocephalic muscle. Furthermore, all thyroid lobes exhibited homogeneous to mildly heterogeneous echotexture. This study establishes diagnostic baselines for thyroid evaluation in the Turkmen horse breed aiding in the detection and management of thyroid pathologies.

title: Arthroscopic Bone Xenograft Augmentation for Glenoid Bone Deficiency and Recurrent Anterior Shoulder Instability Improves Functional Outcomes Despite Graft Nonunion.
abstract: To analyze the healing of equine-derived xenograft bone blocks with the native glenoid using computed tomography (CT) and to evaluate clinical outcomes in patients undergoing arthroscopic bone block stabilization with xenograft, Bankart repair, and upper-third subscapularis tenodesis for recurrent anterior shoulder instability with glenoid bone loss. Patients with recurrent anterior shoulder instability and glenoid bone loss between 12.5% and 25% who underwent arthroscopic equine-derived xenograft bone block augmentation combined with Bankart repair and upper-third subscapularis tenodesis between 2019 and 2023 were identified. Minimum clinical and radiological follow-up was 24 months. Xenograft healing was evaluated on serial CT scans, and clinical outcomes were assessed using Western Ontario Shoulder Instability Index, Rowe, quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand, and visual analog scale scores. A total of 76 patients (72 men, 4 women) met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed, with a mean clinical follow-up of 50.7 months (range, 24-75 months). Radiological follow-up on CT averaged 46.1 months (range, 24-72 months). All patients underwent CT imaging according to the study protocol. Western Ontario Shoulder Instability Index improved from 1335.7 ± 136.8 to 134.6 ± 138.2 (P < .001), with 100% of patients exceeding the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) threshold; Rowe scores increased from 35.3 ± 12.2 to 90.8 ± 11.0 (P < .001), with 100% surpassing the MCID; mean quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand improved from 42.6 ± 21.2 to 4.0 ± 4.7 (P < .001), with 86.8% exceeding the MCID; and visual analog scale decreased from 1.3 ± 1.1 to 0.5 ± 1.1 (P < .001), with 72.4% of patients reaching the MCID. Recurrence occurred in 4 patients (5.3%) because of high-energy trauma, and 2 patients presented Samilson-Prieto grade III osteoarthritis. Despite no radiographic graft-glenoid fusion being observed in any patient (0/76), graft morphology and volume were maintained without signs of resorption throughout follow-up. Despite the lack of radiographic union, most patients treated with arthroscopic bone xenograft plus Bankart repair and upper-third subscapularis tenodesis showed functional improvements surpassing the MCID threshold at a minimum 2-year follow-up. Level IV, retrospective therapeutic case series.

title: Co-encapsulation of Macrotyloma uniflorum protein and Pleurotus ostreatus extract in alginate hydrogels: antioxidant potential and phase-specific bioaccessibility.
journal: Journal of the science of food and agriculture
abstract: The development of sustainable delivery systems for bioactive compounds is essential to improving their physicochemical stability, bioaccessibility and functional properties in food applications. This study aimed to develop sodium alginate-based hydrogel beads through ionic gelation for the co-encapsulation of protein (HP) extracted from germinated Macrotyloma uniflorum seeds and oyster mushroom extract (OME) from Pleurotus ostreatus, thereby creating a hydrogel-based co-encapsulation system. Alginate hydrogel beads containing horse gram protein-oyster mushroom extract (HP-OME) complexes were successfully fabricated across HP:OME weight ratios of 1:0.1 to 1:0.3 (w/w). The beads exhibited uniform mean diameters (2.03-2.23 mm), whereas precursor colloidal suspensions showed good dispersion stability (polydispersity index = 0.28-0.34) and increasingly negative ζ-potential values (-21.40 to -30.90 mV). Encapsulation efficiency increased from 61.7% to 91.5% with increasing OME concentration. Results revealed that HPO-2 (1:0.2 w/w) showed maximum mechanical strength (hardness: 11.23 N), whereas HPO-3 (1:0.3 w/w) exhibited the highest encapsulation efficiency (61.7% to 91.50%), swelling ratio (6.06g/g) and antioxidant activity based on DPPH (i.e. 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl), ABTS [i.e. 2,2'-azino-bis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid)] and FRAP (i.e. ferric reducing antioxidant power) assays. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction analyses indicated non-covalent protein-extract interactions and structural reorganization of the polymer matrix. Simulated static in vitro gastrointestinal digestion showed limited phenolic recovery under gastric conditions and enhanced phase-specific bioaccessibility during the intestinal phase. The co-encapsulated HP-OME hydrogel beads demonstrated high encapsulation efficiency, enhanced antioxidant functionality and favorable phase-specific gastrointestinal bioaccessibility, highlighting their potential as a hydrogel-based co-encapsulation system with customizable mechanical and antioxidant attributes for functional food applications. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: RPA-assisted three-channel Cas13a-Cas13b-Cas12a fluorescence architecture for three-channel viral nucleic acid detection.
abstract: Multiplex nucleic-acid analysis requires orthogonal signal channels capable of resolving multiple targets without substantial cross-interference. Here, an RPA-assisted three-channel CRISPR fluorescence readout was developed by coupling the distinct collateral-cleavage activities of LwaCas13a, PsmCas13b, and LbaCas12a to FAM-, ROX-, and HEX-based reporters, respectively, for detection of Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV), tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV), and an eastern/western equine encephalitis virus (EEEV/WEEV) group target. The corresponding singleplex assays showed no detectable cross-reactivity with the tested non-target viral templates and achieved operational analytical detection limits of 10 copies/μL for VEEV and TBEV and 100 copies/μL for the EEEV/WEEV group assay. Integration of the three Cas-crRNA-reporter modules into one downstream reaction enabled discrimination of single-, dual-, and three-target combinations, with an analytical detection limit of 100 copies/μL for each target in the equal-concentration three-target mixture. Reporter optimization provided balanced channel responses, while inter-day repeatability and interlaboratory reproducibility yielded coefficients of variation below 10%. In a preliminary matrix evaluation using contrived equine nasal-swab samples, plasmid-spiked samples and unspiked negative controls showed concordant classification between the CRISPR readout and RT-qPCR, indicating compatibility of the assay workflow with the tested sample matrix. The method provides a three-channel analytical architecture that consolidates three downstream CRISPR readouts into one reaction while retaining target-assigned fluorescence interpretation.

title: Characterization of EHV-1 viral genes at the respiratory tract using a tracheal explant culture model.
abstract: Equine herpesvirus 1 is the cause of respiratory disease, abortions, and equine herpesvirus myeloencephalopathy (EHM) in horse populations worldwide. Current vaccines do not prevent EHM. Several viral genes have been implicated in systemic dissemination and viral transfer to the CNS, but their roles during early respiratory events remain unclear. This study employed an equine tracheal explant culture model to characterize the role of selected EHV-1 genes in viral replication, infectivity, and innate immune activation during early respiratory infection. Tracheal explants were collected from respiratory healthy horses and inoculated with EHV-1 Ab4 WT or EHV-1 Ab4 recombinant viruses containing deletions or substitutions in genes involved in neuropathogenesis. Viral infection was evaluated using complementary approaches including immunohistochemistry, quantitative PCR, TCID₅₀ assays, and RT-qPCR analysis of innate immune genes. Deletion of ORF1 resulted in increased viral antigen detection, elevated viral DNA levels, enhanced production of infectious virus, and induction of innate immune markers (TLR3, IRF7, IRF9, CXCL9, CXCL10, CCL2, IL-6) supporting the role of ORF1 in modulating epithelial immune responses during early infection. Deletion of ORF2 increased antigen detection and showed limited regulation of chemokines (CXCL9, CCL5). Deletion of the gI-gE heterodimer reduced infectious virus production despite limited effects on viral genome presence, while increasing the expression of TLR3, IRF7, and CXCL9, highlighting its importance in cell-cell spread at the respiratory epithelium. Additionally, gB4, gD4, and the N752 variant exhibited WT-like replication with only subtle immune effects. Collectively, these findings provide insight into viral determinants that shape early epithelial infection and may influence downstream disease outcomes.

title: Molecular Detection of Horse and Goat Meat Using the mtDNA COI Gene in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
abstract: Meat adulteration is a growing concern because it compromises food authenticity, consumer confidence, and ethical or religious preferences. This study aimed to detect goat and horse DNA in meat marketed as goat meat in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, using mitochondrial cytochrome oxidase I (COI)-based polymerase chain reaction (PCR). A cross-sectional study was conducted from August 2025 to March 2026. A total of 427 raw meat samples were collected from licensed butcheries using a multistage random sampling approach. Genomic DNA was extracted using phenol-chloroform and salting-out methods and analyzed by conventional PCR using species-specific primers targeting the mitochondrial COI gene. A structured questionnaire was administered to assess meat-handler awareness of meat adulteration. Of the 427 samples analyzed, 368 (86.2%) were positive for goat DNA, whereas 5 (1.2%) were positive for horse DNA, indicating the presence of undeclared horse-derived genetic material. No amplification was detected in 54 (12.6%) samples, which were classified as inconclusive. Because only five samples were positive for horse DNA, statistical assessment of factors associated with horse DNA detection was not considered sufficiently reliable, and questionnaire findings are therefore presented descriptively. Awareness of meat adulteration was moderate, although the ability to identify adulterated meat by visual inspection alone was limited. Because the assay was qualitative, horse DNA could be detected but not quantified. These findings demonstrate the utility of COI-based PCR for meat species identification and support strengthening surveillance, laboratory capacity, and food authenticity monitoring systems in Ethiopia.

title: Ovarian insufficiency across the lifespan: Diagnosis, Monitoring and HRT controversies.
journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists

title: Targeted Dual-Responsive Probiotic Microspheres for Sequential Protection, Adhesion, and On-Demand Release in Ulcerative Colitis Therapy.
abstract: Oral probiotics show promise for inflammatory bowel disease but are limited by poor gastrointestinal viability, targeting, and colonization. We developed a multi-targeting probiotic composite microsphere (PCM) via scalable solution blow-spinning, with >20-fold higher throughput than electrospinning. PCMs provide three key functions: (1) pH-triggered probiotic protection: PCMs contract in gastric acid, shielding probiotics and increasing survival 2162-fold over free probiotics; (2) charge-mediated adhesion: negatively charged microspheres adhere to positively charged mucin overexpressed at inflamed colonic lesions; and (3) enzyme-triggered release: overexpressed hyaluronidase degrades hyaluronic acid, releasing viable bacteria via the "Trojan horse" mechanism. This sequential mechanism ensures high local probiotic density at inflamed sites. In DSS-induced mouse colitis, PCMs outperformed 5-aminosalicylic acid in alleviating inflammation, repairing the mucosal barrier, and restoring microbial homeostasis. 16S rRNA sequencing showed selective enrichment of beneficial genera and suppression of inflammation-associated pathobionts. This scalable, multi-responsive platform offers next-generation oral therapy for IBD and microbiome-associated gastrointestinal diseases.

title: Ga3+ Replacing of Fe3+ as a "Trojan Horse" Antimicrobial Strategy: Modeling the Process within Bacterial Catalase-Peroxidase KatG.
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
abstract: Replacement of Fe3+ by Ga3+ has emerged as a promising "Trojan horse" antimicrobial strategy in response to the growing threat of antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Because many bacterial proteins hijack host iron to sustain essential redox processes, substitution with redox inactive Ga3+, which closely resembles Fe3+ in ionic radius but possesses only one oxidation state, can disrupt their activity. Among potential targets, bacterial catalase-peroxidase shows particular sensitivity to Fe3+/Ga3+ exchange. However, the structural determinants and thermodynamic driving forces governing this substitution remain poorly understood. Here we combine ad hoc force field development, molecular dynamics simulations, alchemical free energy calculations, and QM/MM methods to elucidate the molecular basis of Fe3+/Ga3+ exchange in the bacterial catalase-peroxidase KatG. Our simulations show that the axial coordination environment of the heme B cofactor is largely preserved upon metal substitution, while the distal ligand dynamically alternates between histidine and a coordinated water molecule. Energy decomposition analysis reveals residue specific differences in electrostatic and van der Waals interactions following metal exchange. Free energy calculations indicate that substitution of iron by gallium in the KatG active site is thermodynamically favorable. The presence of a coordinated water molecule emerges as a key structural feature in both metalated states, while distinct binding patterns contribute differently to the overall thermodynamic driving force. These results provide an atomistic description of gallium mediated metal substitution in KatG and offer mechanistic insight into gallium-based antimicrobial strategies, supporting the rational design of new iron-mimetic antibacterial agents.

title: [Clinical outcomes of horse antithymocyte globulin-based immunosuppressive therapy for aplastic anemia at a single institution].
journal: [Rinsho ketsueki] The Japanese journal of clinical hematology
abstract: Horse antithymocyte globulin (hATG) has been available for the treatment of aplastic anemia (AA) in Japan since 2023. To evaluate the efficacy and safety of combination therapy with hATG, cyclosporine, and a thrombopoietin receptor agonist (TPO-RA), and determine the optimal steroid regimen for serum sickness prophylaxis. We retrospectively reviewed seven patients with AA who received hATG combined with cyclosporine and a thrombopoietin receptor agonist (TPO-RA; eltrombopag or romiplostim). The median age was 62 years. All patients achieved transfusion independence within 3 months (median day 35 for red blood cells and day 36 for platelets). Six patients remain alive and transfusion-independent, while one died of heart failure. The early dose-reduction regimen frequently failed because of serum sickness, necessitating a switch to the conventional method. hATG-based triple therapy led to rapid transfusion independence. Switching TPO-RAs may be effective in patients with a suboptimal response. The conventional method of steroid prophylaxis may be preferable.

title: Pregnancy outcome and associated factors following colic surgery in Thoroughbred broodmares.
journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
abstract: Colic surgery in pregnant broodmares raises concerns not only for maternal survival but also for fetal outcome. Although several studies have reported foaling rates after colic surgery and the influence of perioperative factors on pregnancy outcome, the findings remain inconsistent. This study aimed to determine the foaling rate following colic surgery in Thoroughbred broodmares and to evaluate the effects of perioperative factors and gestational stage on pregnancy outcome. Medical records of Thoroughbred broodmares that underwent colic surgery at Shadai Horse Clinic from 2014 to 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Data collected included mare age, gestational stage, diagnosis category, intraoperative hypotension, hypoxemia, anesthetic maintenance technique (inhalation anesthesia alone or inhalation anesthesia combined with partial intravenous anesthesia), duration of general anesthesia, postoperative administration of altrenogest, postoperative complications (diarrhea and catheter-associated jugular phlebitis), postoperative signs of endotoxemia, and pregnancy outcome. The overall foaling rate was 69.6% (110/158). The occurrence of intraoperative hypotension in late-gestational mares (P=0.036) were significantly associated with negative pregnancy outcome in univariate analysis, whereas most other perioperative factors showed no significant association. The occurrence of intraoperative hypoxemia was significantly higher in the late-gestational mares, however it did not affect pregnancy outcome. In conclusion, the foaling rate following colic surgery in pregnant Thoroughbred broodmares was comparable to that reported in previous studies. These findings suggest that intraoperative hypotension may warrant particular attention in late-gestation mare undergoing colic surgery.

title: Evaluation of linkage disequilibrium, haplotype block structure, and historical effective population size in the Iranian Turkmen horse.
journal: Mammalian genome : official journal of the International Mammalian Genome Society
abstract: This study used the Illumina Equine SNP70 BeadChip to investigate whole-genome linkage disequilibrium (LD), haplotype block structure, and historical effective population size (Ne) of the Iranian Turkmen horse. Genotyping was performed on 70 samples, of which 62 passed quality control and were retained for analysis. We estimated the extent of LD using r2 and D' measures and characterized haplotype block structure and historical Ne. Gene Ontology (GO) and pathway enrichment analyses were performed to identify biological functions associated with genes within the detected haplotype blocks. Across all SNP pairs analyzed (distance ≤ 5 Mb), mean r2 was 0.04, while mean D' was 0.47. Mean r2 for the closest SNP pairs (<5 kb) was 0.49, indicating high LD at short distances. Because D' is sensitive to allele frequency and sample size, the interpretation focused primarily on r2. A total of 5,155 haplotype blocks were detected, mainly on chromosome 1, involving 16,553 SNPs and encompassing 29% of all SNPs in the genome. The estimated Ne decreased with increasing number of generations, indicating the need for adequate conservation measures to ensure the genetic diversity of this valuable breed. GO and pathway enrichment analysis of genes within the longest haplotype blocks showed significant overrepresentation of biological processes related to steroid metabolism, oxidative demethylation, apoptotic signaling, chemical carcinogenesis, and retinol metabolism. These findings suggest candidate biological processes that require further validation.

title: Ecdysterone concentrations in horses following treatment and withdrawal of this naturally occurring prohibited anabolic steroid.
abstract: The medicinal properties of ecdysterone, a steroid made by plants, insects, and internal parasites, have been exploited in traditional medicine for decades. As ecdysterone can increase muscle strength, it could benefit senior horses with muscle wasting. However, the wide availability of ecdysterone supplements is a concern for horseracing authorities, while the risk of environmental exposure to this prohibited substance presents a challenge for owners and trainers. This study examined ecdysterone concentrations in eight Standardbred horses following ecdysterone treatment, re-examined samples from another study using 17 horses, and compared ELISA values with mass spectrometry data to explore some unexpected results. Serum ecdysterone concentrations peaked at 36 ng/mL (median), 40 min after a single oral dose (5 mg/kgBW). A second peak occurred, likely due to enterohepatic recycling, between 2 and 24 h, varying markedly between horses and reaching 9-134 ng/mL. Concentrations returned to pre-treatment values in all horses after 32 h and no accumulation occurred in serum or faeces during 7 daily doses. Serum ecdysterone was persistently high (ca. 20 ng/mL) in one individual when measured by ELISA, but not by mass spectrometry, indicating likely interference with the antibody-based assay. Otherwise, the two analytical methods showed good agreement. Ecdysterone concentrations measured in 17 different horses four times in one day showed marked and sporadic spikes which appeared and disappeared within 40 min, suggesting an endogenous origin (e.g. from internal parasites). Additional studies are needed to understand this phenomenon, assist anti-doping authorities in setting a residue limit, and explore therapeutic opportunities in equine medicine.

title: Psychotropic Drug GST Interactions: In Vitro Inhibition, Molecular Docking, and Translational Potential in Cancer Therapy.
journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
abstract: Psychotropic drugs are widely used to treat mental disorders, but they also influence cellular pathways linked to cancer. One key enzyme, Glutathione S-transferase (GST), is involved in detoxification and drug resistance in tumors, making it a potential target in cancer therapy. This study examined the effects of selected psychotropic agents aripiprazole, fluoxetine hydrochloride, risperidone, haloperidol, and sodium valproate on GST activity derived from equine liver. Enzyme kinetics were assessed in vitro using 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene (CDNB) as the substrate and ethacrynic acid (Kᵢ = 4.7 ± 0.8 nM) as the standard reference inhibitor. IC50 values were determined, and inhibition constants (Kᵢ) were calculated via Lineweaver-Burk plot analysis. The ranked Kᵢ values were as follows: Haloperidol (2.80 ± 1.6 nM) < Ethacrynic acid (4.70 ± 0.8 nM) < Risperidone (4.90 ± 0.39 nM) < Fluoxetine hydrochloride (5.40 ± 1.0 nM) < Aripiprazole (6.10 ± 0.7 nM) < Sodium valproate (386.0 ± 0.0 nM). Haloperidol showed the strongest GST inhibition among the tested drugs, even exceeding ethacrynic acid in binding affinity. This suggests its potential as a GST modulator in cancer therapy. Molecular docking studies revealed that the highest binding affinities were observed for Risperidone and Aripiprazole, showing scores of -7.350 to -7.576 Kcal/mol for 9GSS and -8.786 to -8.982 Kcal/mol for 5JCU. These strong interactions indicate a high potential of both compounds to effectively bind within the GST active site. The molecular dynamics simulation confirmed the stability and consistency of these complexes throughout the simulation period. Given the anticancer role of GST inhibitors, psychotropic drugs with significant GST inhibition especially haloperidol may positively contribute to cancer treatment.

title: Metabolite profiling and in vitro biological activities of an endophytic Cladosporium sp. AUMC 15471 isolated from Origanum syriacum L.
abstract: Endophytic fungi associated with the za'atar plant (O. syriacum L.) remain largely underexplored despite their potential as sources of bioactive natural products. This study aimed to characterize the endophytic fungus Cladosporium sp. AUMC 15471 recovered from Origanum syriacum leaves and to investigate its chemical profile and biological activities. Identification of Cladosporium sp. was achieved by morphological and molecular approaches. Comprehensive metabolite profiling of the ethyl acetate (EtOAc) crude extract was conducted using complementary chromatographic and mass spectrometric techniques, including gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). GC-MS analysis tentatively annotated 32 volatile and semi-volatile compounds based on mass spectral database matching and retention index comparison, predominantly monoterpenes, sesquiterpenes, and fatty alcohols. Targeted LC-MS/MS analysis detected 11 metabolites that were assigned based on retention time and mass-spectrometric characteristics in comparison with authentic reference standards. Several of these metabolites have not previously been reported in an endophytic Cladosporium sp. associated with O. syriacum. The EtOAc crude extract exhibited moderate antioxidant activity in the DPPH assay (IC50 = 230.21 ± 5.96 μg/mL). It also showed low cytotoxic activity against HepG2 hepatocellular carcinoma cells (IC50 = 93.43 μg/mL), with cell death involving both apoptotic and necrotic pathways. In addition, the extract displayed antibacterial activity against six bacterial species comprising five foodborne bacterial pathogens and one an opportunistic equine pathogen, with inhibition rates of 67.37% ± 2.45% against Staphylococcus aureus and 59.39% ± 1.24% against Campylobacter jejuni. Collectively, these findings indicate that Cladosporium sp. associated with O. syriacum is a promising source of chemically diverse metabolites with potential biological activities.

title: In Vivo Metabolic Profiling of Suzetrigine in Thoroughbred Horses Following Oral Administration: Implications for Equine Anti-Doping Control.
abstract: Suzetrigine (VX-548), a selective NaV1.8 sodium channel blocker recently approved for pain management, was investigated for its metabolic fate in Thoroughbred horses using liquid chromatography coupled to high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS). Equine urine and plasma samples were collected following administration and processed prior to analysis. Combining the present in vivo data with earlier reported in vitro liver incubations, a total of 12 metabolites (M1-M12) were identified and characterised, comprising nine Phase I and three Phase II biotransformation products. Five Phase I metabolites (M1-M4 and M9) were detected in vivo, formed through O-demethylation, C-demethylation, monohydroxylation, and hydrolysis of the amide function. Four further Phase I metabolites (M5-M8), previously reported by our team, were observed solely in in vitro liver incubations and were not detected in any in vivo sample. Phase II metabolism yielded three conjugated metabolites, comprising two glycosidation products (M10 and M11) detected in both urine and plasma, and one sulfonate conjugate (M12) confined to urine. Intact suzetrigine was the most abundant plasma analyte at every sampling point, followed by the O-demethylated metabolite M1, whereas in urine, the amide hydrolysis product M9 was overwhelmingly dominant and the parent drug accounted for less than 1% of its response. Intact suzetrigine remained detectable in plasma throughout a 192-h period, while M1 and M9 persisted in urine to the final sampling points. These findings define the metabolic disposition of suzetrigine in the horse and identify M9 and M1 as the most suitable analytical targets for the detection of suzetrigine misuse in equine doping control.

title: Evidence of Coxiella burnetii exposure in equids in Brazil.
abstract: Coxiella burnetii exposure in equids remains poorly investigated worldwide and has never been evaluated in Brazil. To investigate the occurrence of anti-C. burnetii antibodies in a large population of equids from southeastern Brazil and to identify associated risk factors. A cross-sectional study was conducted on 307 apparently healthy equids, including horses, donkeys, and mules, from six municipalities in the Greater Vitória Metropolitan Region, Espírito Santo State, Brazil. Sera were tested for anti-C. burnetii antibodies by indirect immunofluorescence assay (IFA). Univariate analysis was performed to evaluate associations between seropositivity and demographic, environmental, and management variables. Seropositivity was detected in 9.45% (29/307) of the animals. A statistically significant association was observed between location and seropositivity (P = 0.0146), with equids from Vila Velha showing 4.26-fold higher odds of seropositivity than those from the reference municipality. Breeding equids showed higher odds of seropositivity (OR = 1.49), whereas equids with cat contact showed lower odds (OR = 0.45); however, neither association was statistically significant. No significant associations were observed between seropositivity and sex, age, equid type, topography, access to standing water, contact with ruminants, dogs, pigs, poultry, or tick infestation. This study provides the first evidence of exposure to C. burnetii in equids from Brazil. The absence of an association between seropositivity and contact with ruminants, together with the higher seropositivity observed in one municipality, suggests that exposure to C. burnetii may be more closely related to geographic area than to contact with known animal reservoirs.

title: A dietary nutraceutical "Succeed Digestive Conditioning ProgramTM" is more effective than omeprazole for managing equine glandular gastric disease.
abstract: Equine glandular gastric disease (EGGD) responds poorly to proton pump inhibitor therapy, highlighting the need for alternative treatments. Succeed Digestive Conditioning Program (SUC) contains oat-derived ingredients, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, L-glutamine, and L-threonine that may support gastric health. To compare effects of SUC and omeprazole (OME) on squamous and glandular gastric ulcers in horses. Fifty-nine horses with squamous gastric lesions (score ≥2/4) completed a 90-day trial. Horses received either OME (4 mg/kg BW/day; n=30) or SUC (27 g/day; n=29). Forty-four horses had concurrent glandular lesions (OME, n=21; SUC, n=23). Gastroscopy was performed on Days 0, 30, 60, and 90. Squamous lesions were graded using a 0-4 scoring system. Glandular lesions were evaluated using lesion number, lesion severity, and composite ulcer index. Fecal pH was also assessed. OME reduced squamous lesion scores by Day 30 (P<0.001), and scores were lower than SUC horses on Days 30 (P=0.007), 60 (P<0.001), and 90 (P=0.02). SUC had no effect on squamous lesion scores. SUC reduced glandular lesion number scores by Day 60 (P=0.003) and Day 90 (P=0.003), and reduced glandular ulcer index scores by Day 60 (P=0.01) and Day 90 (P=0.03). OME had no effects on any glandular metrics. Neither treatment affected fecal pH. Omeprazole effective reduced squamous gastric lesions but did not improve glandular lesions. In contrast, SUC improved glandular lesion number and ulcer index without affecting squamous disease. SUC may represent a useful strategy for managing EGGD and further investigation into clinical applications are warranted.

title: Physiological impact of reduced anthelmintic intervention in naturally infected Thoroughbred foals: identifying stress indicators of welfare significance.
abstract: Gastrointestinal parasitism is common in pasture-raised foals, yet fecal egg count (FEC) may not reflect its physiological impact. Reduced anthelmintic use therefore requires integrated indicators of health, stress, and resilience. To evaluate associations between FEC, growth, hematology, leukocyte morphology, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), cortisol, and behavior-related observations in naturally infected Thoroughbred foals managed under selective anthelmintic control. Thirty-five foals were followed from birth to 13 months under extensive management in southern Brazil, yielding 348 monthly evaluations. Growth, clinical and behavioral responses, FEC, coproculture, hematology, NLR, serum cortisol, fecal consistency, and anthelmintic efficacy were assessed using nonparametric analyses. Cyathostomins predominated (84.0%), whereas Strongyloides spp. occurred mainly in summer. FEC ranged from 0 to 2,900 eggs/g and varied markedly among individuals. Body weight and wither height increased progressively, with average daily gain exceeding 1.0 kg/day during the first three months. Hematological values were mostly within reference ranges, and leukocyte abnormalities were infrequent (4.21%) and mild. Mean NLR was 1.56 ± 1.03. Cortisol was lower in treated foals (P < 0.001) but was not associated with FEC. No consistent associations were found between FEC and growth, hematology, leukocyte morphology, NLR, cortisol, or fecal consistency. Fecal egg count reduction was 6.6% after ivermectin plus praziquantel and 83.3% after piperazine. Foals maintained growth and physiological stability despite persistent subclinical parasitism. FEC alone was insufficient to indicate physiological or behavior-related impairment or the need for treatment.

title: The horse's hidden threat: occurrence and exposure risks to the tremorgenic alkaloid paxilline in central European grasslands.
abstract: Paxilline is a tremorgenic indole-diterpenoid produced by toxin-producing fungal endophytes in meadows and pastures. It is currently understudied in European grasslands. This study evaluated the occurrence of paxilline in selected European grasslands and estimated the exposure risks for horses. The risk of the paxilline exposure was estimated based on the analyses made from a total of 392 grass samples from grasslands. The grass species of Lolium perenne, Lolium multiflorum, Festuca pratensis, Festuca arundinacea, Festuca rubra, Festuca nigrescens, and Festulolium × loliaceum were sampled from grasslands in Austria (n=42 samples, 1 location), France (n=134, 1 location), Hungary (n=14, 1 location), and Germany (n=192, 4 locations). Concentrations were determined using ultra-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry. Per location and year, the positive samples for paxilline ranged from 0 to 45% of tested samples. Associations with location and plant species were observed (p < 0.001). Model estimates using logistic procedures indicated high likelihoods (up to 75%) for detecting paxilline in certain grasslands, such as in France and Austria, especially for F. rubra, followed by L. multiflorum and L. perenne. Temperatures measured two months before sampling were more positively associated with the concentration of paxilline than that at sampling week. Horses are exposed to paxilline in central European grasslands, but the exposure risk differs with their location and plant species. The study suggests that besides preserving the biodiversity of grasslands, routine monitoring for alkaloid occurrence may be needed, especially when F. rubra, L. multiflorum and L. perenne are present.

title: Investigating horse owners' confidence, ability and knowledge-seeking behaviour in recognising equine lameness.
abstract: Undiagnosed lameness is common in horses, but little is known about which aspects of lameness identification owners find difficult. To explore horse owners' confidence and ability to identify equine lameness, and their knowledge-seeking behaviour. In this cross-sectional online survey, 509 UK horse/pony owners identified lameness from videos of sound, forelimb, hindlimb and bilaterally lame horses, reported their knowledge of clinical signs and knowledge-seeking behaviour, and rated their confidence (1, not confident at all, to 5, very confident). Mixed-effects logistic regression (respondent as random effect) tested whether confidence predicted correct identification. Correct identification was 50.6% (n=256/506) for the sound horse, 50.3% (n=510/1014) for forelimb lameness, 32.3% (n=326/1009) for hindlimb lameness, and 8.9% (n=45/505) for bilateral lameness. Confidence significantly predicted correct limb identification (odds ratio [OR] 1.56, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.43-1.70, P < 0.001), remaining significant after adjusting for case difficulty (OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.30-1.58, P < 0.001), which was a stronger predictor. The most common clinical signs described were 'head nod' (93.7%, n=477/509) and 'hip hike/asymmetry' (77.2%, n=393/509); 'pain expressions' accounted for only 7.4% (n=75/1018) of responses. Owners' main information sources were personal experience (95.7%, n=487/509), vet (63.9%, n=325/509), and coach/trainer (23.6%, n=120/509). Many owners failed to correctly identify the affected limb in hindlimb and bilateral lameness, and rarely used signs such as pain expressions. Confidence significantly predicted correct identification, but case difficulty explained more of the variation in accuracy, highlighting a need for evidence-based resources targeted at less confident or less able owners.

title: Preliminary insights into the association between platelet indices and uterine inflammatory status in cyclic mares.
abstract: Endometritis is a major cause of subfertility in mares and is characterized by uterine inflammation and impaired uterine clearance. Platelets contribute to inflammation, immune regulation and tissue remodeling, and platelet (PLT) indices have emerged as readily available biomarkers of inflammatory conditions; however, their association with endometritis in mares remains poorly understood. This study evaluated the relationship between PLT indices and uterine inflammatory status in cyclic mares. Seventeen cyclic mares were classified into healthy (n = 10) and endometritis (n = 7) groups based on cytological evidence of endometrial inflammation and ultrasonographic detection of intrauterine fluid accumulation. Uterine inflammatory status was characterized by endometrial cytology and ultrasonographic findings, including intrauterine fluid accumulation and endometrial edema. PLT indices were measured using an automated hematology analyzer (ADVIA® 2120i), and plasma estradiol (E2) and progesterone (P4) concentrations were determined. Group comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple testing. Mares with endometritis showed significantly higher PLT count, plateletcrit (PCT), mean platelet volume (MPV), platelet large cell ratio (P-LCR), platelet distribution width (PDW), mean platelet mass (MPM), platelet component distribution width (PCDW) and platelet mass distribution width (PMDW) than healthy mares. All significant differences remained after correction and exhibited large to very large effect sizes. In addition, mares with endometritis showed higher plasma E2 concentrations and lower P4 concentrations than healthy mares. These findings indicate that endometritis is associated with marked alterations in circulating PLT characteristics, particularly in indices related to PLT size, heterogeneity, and mass. PLT indices obtained from routine hematological analyses may represent accessible complementary biomarkers of uterine inflammatory status in mares.

title: Blood serotonin, ionized magnesium, cardiac troponin I, N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide concentrations, and mitral valve billowing in horses with mitral valve regurgitation.
abstract: Serotonin, ionized magnesium (iMg), cardiac biomarkers, and mitral valve prolapse are extensively investigated in humans and dogs with mitral valve regurgitation (MR), but not in horses. To investigate serotonin, iMg, cardiac troponin I (cTnI), and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) concentrations and degree of mitral valve billowing (MVB) in horses with MR. Eighty controls (no/trivial MR), 122 horses with MR (92 mild, 24 moderate, 6 severe). Prospective cross-sectional observational study. All horses underwent echocardiography with MVB distance assessment and MR classification. Platelet-poor plasma serotonin and serum iMg, cTnI, and NT-proBNP concentrations were determined. Controls and horses with different MR grades, biomarker concentrations, and MVB distance were compared using (non-)parametric tests. Ionized magnesium concentration was lower in MR compared to controls (mean difference, 0.03 mmol/L; 95% CI, 0.01-0.05; P = .01), but showed no correlation with billowing distance. The billowing distance was higher in horses with MR than in controls (septal: median difference, 0.2 cm; 95% CI, 0.1-0.3; P < .001; parietal: median difference, 0.3 cm; 95% CI, 0.2-0.3; P < .001), and in horses with a crescendo compared to a holosystolic MR jet (septal: median difference, 0.2 cm; 95% CI, 0.1-0.3; P = .003; parietal: median difference, 0.1 cm; 95% CI, 0.0-0.2; P = .01). No differences in serotonin, cTnI, and NT-proBNP concentrations were detected. Mitral valve billowing is to some extent likely physiological. The association of serotonin and iMg in MVB and MR requires further investigation. Both cTnI and NT-proBNP showed limited use as biomarkers of MR severity. Achtergrondinformatie: Serotonine, geïoniseerd magnesium (iMg), cardiale biomarkers en mitraalklep prolaps werden reeds uitgebreid onderzocht bij mensen en honden met mitraalklep regurgitatie (MR), in tegenstelling tot paarden met MR. Hypothese/Doelstelling: Het onderzoeken van de serotonine, iMg, cardiaal troponine I (cTnI) en N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) concentraties en de mate van bolling van de mitraalklep naar het linker atrium (MVB) bij paarden met MR. Studiepopulatie: Tachtig controle paarden (geen/triviaal MR), 122 paarden met MR (92 mild, 24 matig, 6 erg). Materiaal en methoden: Prospectieve cross-sectionele observationele studie. Alle paarden ondergingen echocardiografie, waarna de mate van MVB gemeten werd en MR classificatie uitgevoerd werd. De concentraties van serotonine in bloedplaatjesarm plasma en van iMg, cTnI en NT-proBNP in serum werden bepaald. Controle paarden en paarden met verschillende MR graden, biomarker concentraties en de mate van MVB werden onderling vergeleken aan de hand van (non-)parametrische testen. Resultaten: De concentratie iMg was lager bij paarden met MR in vergelijking met controle paarden (gemiddeld verschil, 0.03 mmol/L; 95% BI, 0.01-0.05; P = 0.01), maar vertoonde geen correlatie met de mate van MVB. De mate van MVB was hoger bij paarden met MR dan bij controle paarden (septaal: mediaan verschil, 0.2 cm; 95% BI, 0.1-0.3; P < 0.001; pariëtaal: mediaan verschil, 0.3 cm; 95% BI, 0.2-0.3; P < 0.001), en bij paarden met een crescendo MR jet in vergelijking met paarden met een holosystolische MR jet (septaal: mediaan verschil, 0.2 cm; 95% BI, 0.1-0.3; P = 0.003; pariëtaal: mediaan verschil, 0.1 cm; 95% BI, 0.0-0.2; P = 0.01). Er werden geen verschillen gedetecteerd in de concentraties van serotonine, cTnI en NT-proBNP. Conclusies en klinisch belang: De mate van MVB is tot op een bepaalde hoogte waarschijnlijk fysiologisch. De rol van serotonine en iMg in MVB en MR vergt verder onderzoek. Zowel cTnI als NT-proBNP vertoonden een beperkte meerwaarde als biomarkers bij het bepalen van de ernst van MR.

title: Genomic and probiotic characterization of newly isolated Akkermansia strains from camel and horse feces in alleviating obesity and metabolic dysregulation.
abstract: Accumulating evidence points to Akkermansia muciniphila as a promising candidate to improve obesity-associated metabolic disorders. However, studies on the isolation, identification, and functional validation of Akkermansia strains from the intestines of animals occupying specialized ecological niches (such as camel and horse) remain limited. In this study, we isolated an Akkermansia muciniphila strain Muc_T9 and an Akkermansia massiliensis strain Mas_DA from camel and horse feces, respectively. In vitro assessment revealed divergent probiotic adaptive traits between the two strains, particularly in gastrointestinal stress tolerance. Genomic analysis revealed the presence of genes encoding the functionally related effector proteins P9 and Amuc_1100. In high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice, supplementing with Muc_T9 and Mas_DA significantly ameliorated HFD-induced obesity, dyslipidemia, glucose intolerance, and alleviated colonic inflammation and histological damage. Notably, divergent expression patterns of key genes involved in lipid metabolism and adipose tissue remodeling suggest potential differences in host metabolic regulatory modes. Furthermore, both strains restored gut microbial diversity and increased the relative abundance of putative short-chain fatty acids (SCFA)-producing bacteria. Collectively, Muc_T9 and Mas_DA effectively alleviate HFD-induced metabolic disturbances, providing a theoretical foundation for preventing obesity and metabolic diseases. However, due to the relatively short intervention period and the limitations of functional predictions, extended intervention combined with multi-omics approaches is warranted to further clarify the strain-specific regulatory mechanisms and sustained effects.

title: A Paper-Based Electrochemiluminescence Lateral Flow Immunoassay Using Ruthenium Complex Labeling for the Detection of Naja Naja Venom.
abstract: An indirect competitive paper-based electrochemiluminescence (ECL) lateral flow immunoassay was developed for quantitative detection of Naja naja venom. Equine anti-Naja naja venom IgG served as the primary recognition antibody, ruthenium-complex-labeled rabbit anti-equine IgG as the ECL reporter and immobilized three-finger toxin (3FTX) as the competitive antigen. Ruthenium labeling conditions, the co-reactant system, detection membrane, membrane length, and the labeled-secondary-antibody-to-3FTX ratio were optimized. The selected conditions were a Ru-NHS (ruthenium-complex N-hydroxysuccinimide) ester-to-secondary-antibody molar ratio of 160:1 at 25 °C, Elecsys buffer as the co-reactant, Whatman AE 100 as a 1.5 cm detection membrane, and a 3000:1 secondary-antibody-to-3FTX concentration ratio. The whole-venom calibration series was fitted with a decreasing four-parameter logistic model (R2 = 0.9980). Blank-threshold analysis followed by six-run low-concentration verification supported a practical limit of detection of 32 ng/mL. Quantitative verification identified a limit of quantitation (LOQ) of 300 ng/mL and a validated quantitative range of 300-10,000 ng/mL.
